**Surat al-Saff** (The Ranks)

Medinan, according to all scholars.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿O you who believe, why do you say what you do not do?﴾ On this verse there are three opinions:

First: it was revealed concerning a people who said, "If we knew which deeds are most beloved to Allah, we would hasten to them." When the obligation of jihad was revealed, they held back from it. This is reported by Ibn ʿAbbas and Mujahid.

Second: it was revealed concerning a people among whom some men would say, "I fought," when he had not fought; "I thrust," when he had not thrust; "I struck," when he had not struck; "I endured," when he had not endured. This is reported from ʿIkrimah.

Third: it was revealed concerning the hypocrites, who would say to the Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions, "If you go out and fight, we will go out with you and fight." But when they went out, they drew back from them and stayed behind.

Although the apparent meaning of this verse is a rebuke to the one who says what he does not do, the intended meaning is a rebuke to the one who does not do what he said, because the purpose of the verse is to uphold the duties of the bond (al-iltiyam, the cohesion of the community) and not to abandon it.

(p-528)﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in ranks (ṣaffan), as if they were a solid structure.﴾ "In ranks" means arranged in rows, as in prayer, because if they line up, for example, in two rows, they are firmer and more protected from their enemy.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: this is an instruction from Allah to the believers.

﴿As if they were a solid structure (bunyānun marṣūṣ).﴾ On this there are two interpretations:

First: marṣūṣ refers to that which is joined closely together, so that you see no gap or hole in it, because this is firmer in construction than when it is scattered. Likewise are the rows. This is the view of Ibn Jubayr. A poet said:

*And a densely mortared (marṣūṣ) fortress of clay and pebbles, with battlements above them and stone-projections (nasāʾib)*

Second: marṣūṣ refers to that which is built with lead (al-raṣāṣ), as al-Farrāʾ said. From this is the saying of the rajaz poet:

*What the white (blades) suffered from al-Ḥurquṣ, who opens the door of the locked, leaded (marṣūṣ) gate.*

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 61, verses 5–6:

﴿Then when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾ And regarding the word zaygh (deviation) there are two aspects:

One of them: It is swerving (al-'udul), as said by al-Suddi.

The second: It is inclination (al-mayl), except that it is only used for deviation from the truth, not from falsehood.

Its interpretation may bear two meanings:

One of them: When they deviated from obedience, Allah caused their hearts to deviate from guidance.

The second: When they deviated from faith, He caused their hearts to deviate from speech.

(p-529) Regarding those intended by this statement there are three opinions:

One of them: the hypocrites.

The second: the Kharijites, said by Mus'ab ibn Sa'id on the authority of his father.

The third: that it is general.

﴿And a messenger giving good tidings of one who will come after me, whose name is Ahmad﴾ This good tidings from 'Isa includes two matters:

One of them: conveying this to his people so that they would believe in him when he comes. Such conveyance would not come from him, after Allah informed him of that, except by command to convey it to his community.

The second: that this be one of the miracles of 'Isa at the appearance of Muhammad (ﷺ). This is permissible, in that 'Isa may have been limited to being informed of it by Allah without being commanded to convey it.

Regarding Allah's naming him Ahmad there are two aspects:

One of them: because it is one of his names, so he was called Ahmad and Muhammad. Hassan said:

"May God bless, and those who surround His Throne, and the good ones, upon the blessed Ahmad."

The second: that it is derived from his name Mahmud, so the derivation became a name, as Hassan said:

"He derived for him from his name to honour him, so the Lord of the Throne is Mahmud, and this is Muhammad."

It is narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "My name in the Torah is Ahyad, because I save (uhid) my community from the Fire; my name in the Zabur is al-Mahi, for God erased (maha) through me the worship of idols; my name in the Injil is Ahmad; and my name in the Qur'an is Muhammad, because I am praised (mahmud) among the people of the heavens and the earth."

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 61, verses 7–9:

﴿And who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah while he is being invited to Islam?﴾ There are two opinions concerning them:

The first: they are the disbelievers and the hypocrites. This was said by Ibn Jurayj.

The second: he is al-Nadr, who was from the Banu Abd al-Dar, and who said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, al-Uzza and al-Lat will intercede for me." So Allah revealed this verse. This was said by Ikrimah.

﴿They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths﴾ – the verse.

Itfa' (extinguishing) is ikhmad (quenching), and both are used for fire, and they are used metaphorically for what runs in its manner, such as light and radiance.

The difference between itfa' and ikhmad in one respect is that itfa' is used for both little and much, whereas ikhmad is used for much but not for little. One says "atfa'tu al-sirāj" (I extinguished the lamp), and one does not say "akhmadtu al-sirāj" (I quenched the lamp).

As for "the light of Allah" here, there are five opinions:

The first: it is the Qur'an; they want to nullify it by speech. This was said by Ibn Zayd.

The second: it is Islam; they want to repel it by words. This was said by al-Suddi.

The third: it is Muhammad (ﷺ); they want to destroy him by rumours. This was said by al-Dahhak.

The fourth: it is the proofs and signs of Allah; they want to nullify them by their denial and their rejection. This was said by Ibn Bahr.

The fifth: it is a parable struck, meaning: whoever wants to extinguish the light of the sun with his mouth, finds it impossible and unattainable; likewise whoever wants to nullify the truth. This was related by Ibn Isa.

The occasion of revelation of this verse is what Ata related from Ibn Abbas: "The Prophet (ﷺ) was delayed in receiving revelation for forty days, so Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf said: 'O assembly of the Jews, rejoice, for Allah has extinguished the light of Muhammad in what used to descend upon him, and Allah would not complete his affair.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) grieved over that, so Allah revealed this verse, then revelation was connected after it."

﴿That He may make it prevail over all religion﴾ – the verse.

Concerning al-Izhar (making prevail) there are three opinions:

The first: victory over the people of the religions.

The second: exaltation above the religions.

The third: knowledge of the religions, from their saying "qad zahartu 'ala sirrihi" (I came to know his secret), meaning I came to know it.

Another [favour] you love: help from Allah and a near victory. This is from Allah to increase the encouragement, because when He promised them Paradise in return for obedience to Him and to His Messenger, it was known that among them were those who wanted swift help, out of desire for worldly gain and for the strengthening of the religion. So He promised them what would strengthen their desire, and said: ﴿Another [favour] you love: help from Allah and a near victory﴾. He means the conquest of lands, for Him and for them. Allah fulfilled His promise in both matters, the help and the victory.

Regarding His words ﴿near﴾ there are two views:

The first: it refers to what they love, that it is help from Allah and a near victory.

The second: it is a report from Allah that what they love of that will come soon, and so it happened, for He hastened the conquest and the victory for them.
